own_solution.law: At constant speed, the load's kinetic energy is unchanged. The motor supplies gravitational work W = mgh, so average mechanical power P = mgh/t = 80 × 9.8 × 6/10 = 470.4 W.
assumptions: Gravity is uniform at the stated value.
A box attached for the present lift becomes part of the total lifted load.

TEC7E.regime: The stated constant-speed lift is feasible when the available mechanical power is at least mgh/t; 930 W exceeds the required 470.4 W.

T635D.regime: The stated constant-speed lift is feasible when the available mechanical power is at least mgh/t; 930 W exceeds the required 470.4 W.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T4034 and T3979 replace the specified 12 kg box with an unspecified 'small box', so the box-mass variants do not all preserve the required number and unit.

counterexamples: A 5 kg small box satisfies T4034 or T3979, demonstrating that neither sentence preserves the 12 kg mass specified in the other box variants.
notes: The base problem and every individual augmented problem have determinate power answers. The invalid verdict concerns the required preservation of quantity across variants. The unspecified box masses in T4034 and T3979 do not affect their answers because those boxes are disconnected from the present lift. With an attached 12 kg box, power is (80 + 12) × 9.8 × 6/10 = 540.96 W. Initial absolute height cancels in mg[(y0 + 6) − y0].
